lessons.title: Parallel Execution with Promise.all()
lessons.description: Run multiple async operations simultaneously and wait for all of them to complete.

sections.heading: Promise.all()
paragraphs: Promise.all() takes an array of Promises and returns a new Promise that resolves when all of them resolve. If any one rejects, the whole thing rejects.
list: Resolves with an array of results (same order as input)
Rejects immediately if ANY Promise rejects
All operations run in parallel — not sequentially

codeExamples.heading: Parallel fetching with Promise.all
explanation: Promise.all runs all fetches simultaneously — total time = slowest request.
Sequential awaits wait for each to finish before starting the next.
Promise.all is dramatically faster when requests are independent.
If any request fails, Promise.all rejects immediately.

practice.task: Fetch 3 different endpoints in parallel using Promise.all. Measure the total time vs sequential fetching.
hints: Compare parallel vs sequential total time.

keyTakeaways: Promise.all runs multiple Promises in parallel.
Results come back as an array in the same order as the input.
If any Promise rejects, the whole Promise.all rejects.
Use Promise.all for independent async operations to maximize speed.
lessons.challenge: Fetch data from 5 endpoints in parallel and render the results on the page as they arrive.

lessons.title: Fault-Tolerant Concurrent Operations with Promise.allSettled()
lessons.description: Wait for all Promises to settle — success or failure — without short-circuiting on the first error.

sections.heading: Promise.allSettled()
paragraphs: Promise.allSettled() waits for all Promises to complete (fulfilled or rejected) and returns the status of each. It never rejects.
list: Returns an array of status objects: {status: "fulfilled", value} or {status: "rejected", reason}
Use when you need results from all operations regardless of failures

codeExamples.heading: Promise.allSettled() in action
explanation: Promise.allSettled waits for all operations to finish.
Each result has a status: "fulfilled" or "rejected".
Fulfilled results have a value; rejected have a reason.
No matter how many fail, the function resolves with all results.

practice.task: Use Promise.allSettled to fetch 3 endpoints, one of which will fail. Log the status of each result.

keyTakeaways: Promise.allSettled waits for all Promises to settle — it never rejects.
Each result includes status (fulfilled/rejected) and the value or reason.
Use it when you need partial results — some failures are acceptable.
Promise.all is for "all or nothing"; allSettled is for "best effort."
lessons.challenge: Build a dashboard that loads data from multiple APIs and shows whatever loads successfully, even if some fail.

lessons.title: Handling Race Conditions with Promise.race() & Promise.any()
lessons.description: Race multiple Promises — race() returns the first to settle, any() returns the first to succeed.

sections.heading: Promise.race()
list: Returns the result of the FIRST Promise to settle (fulfilled or rejected)
If the first to settle rejects, race() rejects
Useful for timeouts and competing requests

sections.heading: Promise.any()
list: Returns the result of the FIRST Promise to FULFILL
Useful when you have multiple fallback sources
Rejects with AggregateError if all Promises reject

codeExamples.heading: Race and any in action
explanation: Promise.race returns whichever settles first — success or failure.
The timeout pattern races fetch against a timer — if the timer wins, it rejects.
Promise.any returns the first SUCCESS — rejections are ignored.
Promise.any only rejects if ALL Promises reject.

practice.task: Write a fetchWithTimeout function using Promise.race that rejects if the request takes more than 3 seconds.
hints: Create a timeout Promise: new Promise((_, rej) => setTimeout(() => rej(new Error("Timeout")), 3000)).
Race it against the fetch Promise.
If the timeout wins, the error is thrown.

keyTakeaways: Promise.race returns the first to settle — success or failure.
Promise.any returns the first to succeed — it ignores rejections.
Use race for timeouts: race a fetch against a timer.
Use any for fallback sources: try multiple mirrors/APIs.
lessons.challenge: Build a function that tries 3 API mirrors using Promise.any, with a 5-second timeout using Promise.race.
